claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Intermediate annealing near 900°C promotes nanoscale chemical short-range order.
Changing annealing time at approximately 900°C can vary the extent of short-range order.
The proposed experiment uses annealing durations of 0, 10, 30, and 60 minutes at approximately 900°C followed by rapid quenching.
Immediate quenching from the high-temperature state suppresses short-range-order formation.
The proposed structural mediator consists of nanoscale Al-enriched clusters exhibiting chemical short-range order.
Al atoms promote local short-range ordering during intermediate annealing.
Al-induced short-range order lowers the nucleation barrier for transformation of the metastable BCC phase.
Short-range ordering locally modifies the free-energy landscape and destabilizes the metastable BCC structure.
The lowered nucleation barrier facilitates transformation into equilibrium FCC or intermetallic phases.
Longer intermediate annealing produces more developed short-range order.
Samples with more developed short-range order will exhibit earlier-onset phase transformation during subsequent low-temperature exposure.
Samples with more developed short-range order will undergo more extensive phase transformation during subsequent low-temperature exposure.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to annealing near 900°C and time scales that produce measurable short-range order.
Deformation and vacancy effects are to be controlled or minimized.
Absence of a systematic association between greater short-range-order intensity and accelerated or more extensive transformation relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
